en.title: Bradley Cooper to Lead Danny McBride's G.I. Joe, Transformers Crossover Canceled
en.summary: The planned cinematic universe merging G.I. Joe and Transformers has been scrapped. Instead, Paramount is focusing on a standalone G.I. Joe film, with Bradley Cooper set to star as Duke and Danny McBride directing.
en.body:
The ambitious plan to unite the worlds of **G.I. Joe** and **Transformers** on the big screen has officially been shelved. Paramount has decided to "uncouple" the beloved Hasbro franchises, signaling an end to the much-anticipated crossover movie that was first teased in 2024. Instead, the focus will shift to a standalone **G.I. Joe** film, helmed by director **Danny McBride**, who is making his feature directorial debut. 

Adding significant star power to this new direction, **Bradley Cooper** is slated to portray the iconic leader of the **G.I. Joe** team, Duke, also known as First Sergeant Conrad S. Hauser. Cooper's casting suggests a character interpretation that leans into the "maverick" qualities previously associated with Duke, a persona that aligns well with the actor's established range. While details about the plot remain scarce, the film is expected to center on the elite commando strike force and will likely feature the perennial antagonists, Cobra Command, as their involvement is almost synonymous with any **G.I. Joe** narrative. **Danny McBride** co-wrote the script with **John Carcieri** and **Jeff Fradley**, and his involvement as director promises a unique comedic and dramatic sensibility.

## A New Mission for G.I. Joe

The decision to cancel the **Transformers**/**G.I. Joe** crossover, which was reportedly being penned by **Jurassic World** writer **Derek Connolly** as recently as June, marks a significant shift in strategy for Paramount. The studio seems to be opting for a more focused approach, allowing each franchise to develop independently. This move may come as a relief to fans who were apprehensive about a potentially crowded narrative, preferring to see their favorite characters explored in dedicated stories. The **G.I. Joe** franchise has a long history, spanning animated series, numerous comic book runs, and several previous film adaptations, some of which have been met with mixed reception. This new iteration, with **McBride** directing and **Cooper** leading the charge, offers a fresh start and a chance to revitalize the property for a new generation of fans.

## What's Next for the Joes

With **Bradley Cooper** confirmed as Duke and **Danny McBride** at the helm, momentum is expected to build for this new **G.I. Joe** film. While specific plot details and a release date have not yet been announced, the swift casting and directorial commitment suggest that development is moving forward with urgency. Fans will be eager to see how McBride and Cooper will reimagine the classic commando team and whether this reboot can capture the enduring appeal of the **G.I. Joe** universe.

In previous iterations of the character, Duke was a bit of a maverick, which fits into Cooper’s acting wheelhouse. News about the live-action film about the popular run of Mattel toys, which has already spawned a very popular animated series, a bunch of comics, and other, less-than-great movie adaptations, is scarce, though it’s supposed to focus on the commando strike force, which Duke was part of. Cobra Command will also likely be involved, because can there be a G.I. Joe movie without Cobra? McBride will be directing in his feature debut, and he wrote the script with John Carcieri and Jeff Fradley. This movie also appears to be free of Transformers; Deadline also reported that the G.I. Joe and Transformers crossover movie announced in 2024 is no longer a going concern, and this Cooper-starring G.I. Joe project has taken its place. Other than that, however, there’s no news on what the plot of the film will be, but given that McBride and Cooper are now on board, odds are good that this project will be moving through development and into production sooner rather than later.
